method: The 96 candidate IDs are reconciled against the current catalog, including aliases and instrument parts. Entries describe selected configurations, not exhaustive cultural inventories. Sources establish repertoire, instruments and performance context. Numeric axes, optional sound controls and the contemporary field-recording chain are authored recording-model choices. Performer-relative tuning records missing interval evidence without asserting 12-TET or just intonation. Coordinates are approximate cultural or documentation anchors and have not received the separate human atlas audit.

entries.notes: Relative size and ensemble role are documented; precise shell species and tuning are not asserted.
One selectable instrument represents the documented pair, preserving the three-drum total with ingina.
Two- and three-string lute recordings are separately catalogued by CREM; string material is left unspecified.
Museum distinguishes secular tune-playing from sacred harp and zither uses; do not automatically place this fiddle in the bear-festival roster.
Default represents the documented three-drum group; goatskin is the contemporary head choice.
Distinct from the Bashkir mouth harp sharing the name kubyz.
The documented ensemble credits establish this drum; unspecified material and tuning remain unspecified.
Separate from the plucked lute called tanbur.
Construction follows NMAI object 275934; precise drum dimensions vary among makers.
The album identifies muganda and chandi; the selected track documents a bass and cylindrical drum alongside twelve singing horns.
Neutral drum abstraction for archival credits that do not identify a local type. Used for Tibesti terdegna and Kiribati batere, not a claim that their drums are identical.
Nyele are edge-blown flutes made from horns, not lip-vibrated brass. The museum attribution of its individual object is tentative.
Community film S33 anchors handgame use; X6 documents Dene drum-making without generalizing one maker’s wood or hide species to all Dene drums.
Two drummers are credited in the documented troupe; precise drum subtype is not inferred from a generic credit.
